This rule compares each file with what `bun format` prints and reports every place where they differ. Formatting problems then show up next to your lint problems, in the terminal and in the editor.

It reads the same settings as `bun format`: your `.prettierrc`, `.editorconfig`, and the `[format]` section of `bunfig.toml`. It skips the files that `bun format` skips. The options and the messages are the same as for `prettier/prettier`, and you do not need Prettier installed.

A file that Bun cannot format the way your config asks, for example because of a Prettier plugin that `bun format` does not have, gets one report that says why.

`--fix` formats the file.

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad */}
```js
const user = {name:'Ada'}
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}
```js
const user = { name: "Ada" };
```

## Options

The first option is an object of formatting options, with the names they have in a `.prettierrc`. They win over your config files.

```toml bunfig.toml
[lint.rules]
"bun/format" = ["error", { singleQuote = true, semi = false }]
```

{/* good {"options": [{"singleQuote": true, "semi": false}]} */}
```js
const user = { name: 'Ada' }
```

{/* bad {"options": [{"singleQuote": true, "semi": false}]} */}
```js
const user = { name: "Ada" };
```

The second option is an object with these keys:

| Option | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `usePrettierrc` | `true` | Read config files such as `.prettierrc` and `.editorconfig`. |
| `fileInfoOptions` | `{}` | `ignorePath` names the ignore file or files to read. `withNodeModules: true` also checks files in `node_modules`. |

## When not to use it

If `bun format --check` already runs in CI, this rule does the same work a second time.
